bibliography.abstract: Transportation planning has traditionally required substantial expertise in network modeling, traffic assignment, and optimization. As a result, strategic analyses such as network design, capacity expansion, and model calibration remain inaccessible to non-expert decision makers. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) provide an opportunity to bridge this gap by enabling natural-language interaction with complex transportation planning tools. However, existing LLM-based systems primarily serve as interfaces to simulation software and lack the ability to efficiently search, evaluate, and optimize transportation solutions. This study proposes an integrated human-AI transportation planning framework that combines a large language model, a model context protocol (MCP) interface, an open-source transportation planning engine (AequilibraE), and a differentiable user equilibrium (UE) assignment layer. The framework allows non-expert users to execute network analyses and improve solutions for optimization. A differentiable UE layer is developed by directly differentiating the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions of the Beckmann traffic assignment problem. The proposed framework is demonstrated through two representative planning tasks: calibration of travel time functions from observed traffic counts and network design under budget constraints. The examples illustrate how differentiable transportation models and LLM agents can jointly democratize transportation planning and substantially reduce barriers between domain expertise and transportation decision making.
bibliography.title: Large Language Model Assisted Transportation Planning through a Differentiable User Equilibrium Layer

en.what: This study presents an integrated transportation planning framework that couples a large language model with the open-source AequilibraE engine and a newly developed differentiable user equilibrium layer based on the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions of Beckmann's assignment problem. The system was validated across two core tasks: calibrating travel time functions against real-world traffic counts and optimizing network capacity expansions under strict budget constraints.
en.why: This approach enables non-expert decision makers to perform automated, gradient-based network design and parameter calibration using natural language instead of relying on external manual optimization scripts.
